CheckTitle: Elastic Beanstalk environment has no sensitive credentials in configuration settings
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: Elastic Beanstalk environment configuration settings (option settings) are inspected for hardcoded secrets, such as API keys, tokens, or passwords embedded in environment configuration.
Risk: Plaintext secrets in Elastic Beanstalk environment configuration settings can be viewed by anyone with read access to the Elastic Beanstalk console or API, exposing downstream resources and integrations.

Code.Other:
1. Open the AWS Elastic Beanstalk console and select your environment.
2. Go to Configuration > Software > Edit.
3. Review the Environment Properties section for any plaintext secrets.
4. For actual secrets, migrate them to AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and reference them securely.

Recommendation.Text: Avoid storing secrets in plaintext in Elastic Beanstalk environment configuration settings. Store sensitive settings securely in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or AWS Secrets Manager.
